- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) or shows strong negative momentum, reduce forecasted peaks and avoid over-optimistic spikes.  
- If model forecasts show a sharp upward spike followed by a steep decline, cap the peak and adjust downward by 5–15% to account for mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending upward, allow for a slight overshoot but cap the 30-day forecast at 10–15% above recent 18-day average to avoid overcorrection.  
- If the last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum (e.g., 2–3 consecutive drops >2% or sentiment <0.2), reduce forecasted highs and shift mean toward lower end of recent range.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the model’s first 5–7 days are significantly above true outcome, apply a “lag correction” by subtracting 10–20% from early forecast values to align with observed price lag.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), avoid smooth extrapolation; use a “sentiment-weighted average” of recent 7-day price and sentiment to anchor forecast midpoints.
